html:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is a world body, based in Washington, that lends to countries that run out of foreign currency and watches over the world's money system. Almost every country is a member.

It was agreed at the Bretton Woods conference of July 1944, along with the World Bank, from plans by the American Harry Dexter White and the British economist John Maynard Keynes. The aim was to avoid the currency wars and collapse of the 1930s. At first it policed a system of fixed exchange rates tied to the US dollar, which was tied to gold. That system ended in the early 1970s, and the IMF became mainly a lender of last resort.

Its loans come with conditions, often cuts in spending and subsidies, higher interest rates and opening to trade, and these have made it controversial:

  • In Egypt, price rises agreed with the IMF set off the bread riots of 1977.
  • In 1991 India turned to it in a foreign currency crisis, part of the start of economic liberalisation.
  • In the Asian financial crisis of 1997 it lent huge sums to Thailand, Indonesia and South Korea; critics said its harsh terms deepened the slump.

Votes in the IMF follow each country's share of money paid in, so the United States and Europe hold the most say, and by custom its head has always been a European.
sum: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is a world body, based in Washington, that lends to countries that run out of foreign currency and watches over the world's money system. Almost every country is a member.
